newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico publishes rules for radio frequency bidding.
newsitem.headline: Mexico publishes rules for radio frequency bidding.

text.p: Mexico's Federal Telecommunications Commission (Cofetel) on Monday published rules for bidding on the privatization of radio frequencies.
The rules, published in the Official Gazette (Diario Oficial), said Cofetel would auction the use of the frequencies for a period of 20 years.
On offer at the auctions will be the following regional mobile and fixed wireless frequencies:
--30 megahertz (mhz) concessions in the band between 1850 mhz and 1990 mhz;
--10 mhz concessions in the band between 1850 and 1990 mhz;
--50 mhz concessions in the band between 3.4 and 3.7 gigahertz (ghz);
--and 14 mhz concessions in the bands between 440 and 450 mhz and between 485 and 495 mhz.
Bidding will be carried out according to a complex calender published in the Official Gazette on April 25, Cofetel said.
Requirements for bidding will be published on June 30 in the Official Gazette, a major Mexican newspaper and on the Coftel home page (http://www.cofetel.gob.mx/subasta/espectro/)
